evidence_quotes: 150 seismic events of magnitude 4.0 or greater were recorded between 2026-01-17 and 2026-02-15, averaging 4.62 magnitude
Tobelo, Indonesia (19 events) and Mohr, Iran (15 events)
a magnitude 5.7 on 2026-02-14 at 152.9 km depth and a magnitude 4.5 at only 3.3 km depth on the same date
a magnitude 4.9 at 8.5 km depth on 2026-02-12 and a separate magnitude 4.1 at 1.9 km depth
depths ranging from 11.4 km to 146.2 km
daily event counts spiked to 9 on both 2026-02-03 and 2026-02-14
the shallow 13.6 km depth recorded near Lata on 2026-02-14
The dataset covers a 30-day window from 2026-01-17 to 2026-02-15
criticisms: The report states the period covers '2026-01-17 and 2026-02-15' but the digest endtime is 2026-02-16; this is a minor discrepancy — the last daily_counts entry is 2026-02-15 with 6 events, so the report's end date is defensible but slightly inconsistent with the metadata endtime of 2026-02-16.

The report attributes the M5.2 event '65 km E of Aleutian Islands, Alaska' to the Nikolski, Alaska cluster ('an additional magnitude 5.2 event recorded 65 km east of the Aleutian Islands on 2026-02-15, consistent with sustained subduction-zone activity'). While geographically plausible, the digest lists this as a separate place ('65 km E of Aleutian Islands, Alaska'), not as part of the Nikolski count of 13. This conflation could mislead readers about the Nikolski event count.

The report says 'nearly a quarter of all recorded activity' for Tobelo (19) + Mohr (15) = 34 out of 150, which is 22.7% — this is borderline for 'nearly a quarter' (25%) but is a minor rounding/framing issue rather than a fabrication.

The dataset maximum magnitude of 6.2 is cited but no sample event in the digest shows a 6.2 event; it appears only in summary.max_magnitude. The report does not fabricate a specific event for it, but readers may wonder which event it was — this is a transparency gap, not a factual error.
